goal.objective:
`src/cli.js` is the program; how the work is split across other files under `src/` is up to you. It takes exactly one argument, `rounds` or `tally`, and reads an election from standard input. Split the input on newlines and drop the empty tail a trailing newline leaves. Trim each line; ignore it when it is empty or begins with `#`; otherwise split it on runs of whitespace. Exit 0 whenever the election parses.

The line `candidates <name>...` declares the field. It must appear exactly once, before any ballot, and must name at least one candidate; a name is one or more of the characters `A` to `Z`, `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, `_` and `-`, and no name may repeat. The line `ballot <count> <candidate>...` records `count` identical ballots ranking those candidates from most to least preferred. The count is a decimal integer of at least 1 written without a sign and without a leading zero, a ballot names at least one candidate, every name must have been declared, and no ballot may name a candidate twice. A ballot need not rank every candidate.

Count in rounds. Every candidate starts continuing. In each round every ballot counts for the first candidate on it that is still continuing; a ballot whose named candidates are all eliminated is exhausted and counts for nobody. Let the active total be the number of ballots that counted for someone. When the active total is 0 the election ends with no winner. When some candidate's count, doubled, is greater than the active total, that candidate wins and the election ends. Otherwise exactly one candidate is eliminated and another round is counted.

The candidate eliminated is the one with the fewest votes in this round. When several tie for fewest, compare them across the rounds already counted, this one included, from the first round onwards: at the first round where their counts are not all equal, keep only those with the fewest votes in that round and compare the survivors the same way from the first round again. When no round separates them, eliminate the one whose name sorts last by code point.

`rounds` prints, for each round in order, `round K: ` followed by one `<name>=<votes>` for every continuing candidate, separated by single spaces, and then `exhausted=<n>`. Candidates are listed by descending vote count, and by ascending name where counts tie. A round that eliminated someone is followed by the line `eliminated <name>`. `tally` instead prints one line, `rounds N`, holding how many rounds were counted. Both modes end with `winner <name>`, or `no winner` when no candidate ever reached the majority.

A failure writes one line to standard error and exits 2, having written nothing to standard output; stop at the first one. The messages are `error: usage: cli.js rounds|tally` when the argument is not exactly one of the two mode words; `error: line N: candidates must be declared once, before any ballot`; `error: line N: expected candidates <name>...`; `error: line N: invalid candidate name <name>`; `error: line N: candidate <name> is declared twice`; `error: line N: expected ballot <count> <candidate>...`; `error: line N: count must be a positive integer`; `error: line N: unknown candidate <name>`; `error: line N: candidate <name> is repeated`; `error: line N: unknown directive <word>`; and `error: no candidates`, with no line number, when the input declares none. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root. tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

goal.objective:
`src/cli.js` is the program; how the work is split across other files under `src/` is up to you. It takes exactly one argument, `rounds` or `tally`, and reads an election from standard input. Split the input on newlines and drop the empty tail a trailing newline leaves. Trim each line; ignore it when it is empty or begins with `#`; otherwise split it on runs of whitespace. Exit 0 whenever the election parses.

The line `candidates <name>...` declares the field. It must appear exactly once, before any ballot, and must name at least one candidate; a name is one or more of the characters `A` to `Z`, `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, `_` and `-`, and no name may repeat. The line `ballot <count> <candidate>...` records `count` identical ballots ranking those candidates from most to least preferred. The count is a decimal integer of at least 1 written without a sign and without a leading zero, a ballot names at least one candidate, every name must have been declared, and no ballot may name a candidate twice. A ballot need not rank every candidate.

Count in rounds. Every candidate starts continuing. In each round every ballot counts for the first candidate on it that is still continuing; a ballot whose named candidates are all eliminated is exhausted and counts for nobody. Let the active total be the number of ballots that counted for someone. When the active total is 0 the election ends with no winner. When some candidate's count, doubled, is greater than the active total, that candidate wins and the election ends. Otherwise exactly one candidate is eliminated and another round is counted.

The candidate eliminated is the one with the fewest votes in this round. When several tie for fewest, compare them across the rounds already counted, this one included, from the first round onwards: at the first round where their counts are not all equal, keep only those with the fewest votes in that round and compare the survivors the same way from the first round again. When no round separates them, eliminate the one whose name sorts last by code point.

`rounds` prints, for each round in order, `round K: ` followed by one `<name>=<votes>` for every continuing candidate, separated by single spaces, and then `exhausted=<n>`. Candidates are listed by descending vote count, and by ascending name where counts tie. A round that eliminated someone is followed by the line `eliminated <name>`. `tally` instead prints one line, `rounds N`, holding how many rounds were counted. Both modes end with `winner <name>`, or `no winner` when no candidate ever reached the majority.

A failure writes one line to standard error and exits 2, having written nothing to standard output; stop at the first one. The messages are `error: usage: cli.js rounds|tally` when the argument is not exactly one of the two mode words; `error: line N: candidates must be declared once, before any ballot`; `error: line N: expected candidates <name>...`; `error: line N: invalid candidate name <name>`; `error: line N: candidate <name> is declared twice`; `error: line N: expected ballot <count> <candidate>...`; `error: line N: count must be a positive integer`; `error: line N: unknown candidate <name>`; `error: line N: candidate <name> is repeated`; `error: line N: unknown directive <word>`; and `error: no candidates`, with no line number, when the input declares none. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
